messages:
incident-bot: Pager SEV2 — private-vpc vc-12a34: high rate of egress timeouts from dedicated pools (dp-7) to external model registry and telemetry endpoints. Alerts: connection-timeout > 30s across targets. Auto-escalation: paging on-call SRE.

alice.ops: taking this. saw the pager, switching to incident channel. any visible deploys?

sam-support: customer reported 'model load failures' and 502s in their app around 09:42 UTC. Customer: AuroraCorp (dedicated private VPC). They say errors spike when calls hit dedicated pool dp-7.

ben-net: I can start with network checks. initial suspicion: egress control (SG/NACL) or NAT gateway exhaustion.

carmen-sre: quick triage: from a healthy host in vc-12a34_us-east-1 tried `curl -v https://models.example.org/health` and saw: `connect to models.example.org port 443: Operation timed out`. DNS resolves locally to 52.14.22.11.

ryan-platform: ping to resolver 10.0.0.2 (VPC resolver) responded, but `dig +short models.example.org @10.0.0.2` intermittently times out. suggests DNS upstream or SG blocking UDP 53 egress.

alice.ops: runbook step 1: verify SG outbound rules on the interface for dp-7.

ben-net: confirmed: security-group sg-0a1b2c outbound allows 443 only to specific CIDR ranges (customer whitelisted). The model registry IPs are not in that list (we use dynamic IPs). There's also a tighter egress policy applied by infra policy engine earlier today.

sam-support: customer note: they rotated nat gateway yesterday and asked for a targeted firewall policy; we rolled a restrictive SG change at 08:10 UTC. could be related.

carmen-sre: quick mitigation idea: temporarily open outbound 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 on sg-0a1b2c for dp-7 so model registry calls can succeed while we prepare a safer whitelist. I'll queue that action — need approval from on-call.

alice.ops: agree to temporary broad egress while we investigate. mark as mitigation and document. set TTL 15m.

ben-net: I'll patch SG now. executing: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0`

incident-bot: Note: change recorded to infra-audit (runbook:temporary-egress).

carmen-sre: after change, reran `curl` from dp-7 host — model registry now responds 200. customer reports partial recovery but telemetry still shows some failures.

ryan-platform: telemetry indicates heavy retries from dp-7 to internal telemetry collector at 10.2.5.13:443 failing with TLS handshake timeouts. That collector is reachable via private route through NLB (nlb-aug). Need to check NLB target health.

ben-net: checking NLB target group tg-09: several targets show Unhealthy with reason: timeout (health check). The target health check endpoint is 10.2.5.13:9000/health (TCP).

alice.ops: are the NLBs in the same private subnets? any route table changes?

ben-net: route tables look unchanged. But I spotted that the SG change we applied only modified sg-0a1b2c (pods outbound) and didn't touch the NLB's security groups. NLB has its own SGs on host-based endpoints; there was an earlier NACL change affecting ephemeral ports in the subnets (rule 100 denies high ports >1024 temporarily). That would break return path for health checks/ephemeral connections.

carmen-sre: ok that matches: health checks are TCP from nlb to targets on ephemeral >1024. If NACL blocks those, NLB sees timeouts.

sam-support: customer impact: most customer API calls to model registry recovered after sg change, but internal telemetry and long-lived streaming to external analytics remain flaky. We should bring NLB targets back healthy asap.

ben-net: temporary fix: relax NACL rule 100 to allow ephemeral ports 1024-65535 between the affected subnets. I'll apply change and monitor. Command: `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0ff --rule-number 100 --protocol -1 --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress false --cidr-block 10.0.0.0/16 --rule-action allow` (applied).

incident-bot: Change applied to NACL acl-0ff by ben-net at 09:56 UTC.

carmen-sre: NLB target health is recovering: targets now show Healthy after two consecutive checks. Telemetry backlog draining.

alice.ops: great. next steps: 1) keep the temporary SG 443 open but schedule narrow whitelist update with model registry IP prefixes 2) remove the NACL relaxation after cleanup window 3) post-incident follow-up to review change that added restrictive NACL earlier today.

ryan-platform: I'll open a short-lived route and nat check: confirmed no NAT IP exhaustion (CloudWatch NATGatewayBytes/ActiveFlow counts normal). Looks like root cause chain: over-restrictive SG + NACL change + NLB healthchecks on ephemeral ports.

sam-support: customer facing update prepared: "We observed an internal network policy change that briefly prevented internal load-balancer health checks and external egress to dynamic model registry IPs. We applied temporary egress and NACL relaxations which restored service. Working on least-privilege whitelist and rollback plan." Want to send now?

alice.ops: send the update. mention ETA for permanent fix (3 hours) and that we will rotate credentials if any suspicious activity seen. add postmortem owner: carmen-sre.

sam-support: posted to customer at 10:05 UTC and scheduled a call with AuroraCorp for 10:30 to walk through mitigation and permanent plan.

ben-net: I'll start creating an allowlist for the registry domains and add to infra policy engine so future auto-enforcement picks them up. Also will add a test to canary that validates NLB health-check paths after NACL/SG changes.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to MITIGATED by alice.ops at 10:07 UTC. Followup tasks created: #1234 whitelist registry, #1235 revert NACL and schedule maintenance window, #1236 retro-run runbook in staging.

carmen-sre: quick post-checks: ran `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53 or port 443` during window and saw DNS queries to 10.0.0.2 dropped until SG change. snippet of `tcpdump` output: 
```
09:49:12.123456 IP 10.0.1.45.53214 > 10.0.0.2.53: 12345+ A? models.example.org. (38)
09:49:12.223789 IP 10.0.1.45.53214 > 10.0.0.2.53: . RST,ack 0 win 0
09:50:01.987654 IP 10.0.1.45.51234 > 52.14.22.11.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
```

alice.ops: good capture. For the postmortem, please include timeline, exact config diffs (SGs, NACLs) and proposed automation: block-change-review for NACLs, runbook auto-tests. Carmen owns postmortem, Ben owns whitelist task.

sam-support: customer call done — AuroraCorp appreciates speed. they asked for private peering to registry to avoid public IP churn; we'll evaluate.

ben-net: action items pinned. I'll also add an alert to detect NLB target group Unhealthy count > 1 for dedicated pools and auto-notify network team with higher priority.

alice.ops: closing incident thread. thanks all :tada:

incident-bot: Thread closed by alice.ops at 10:12 UTC. Incident ticket: INC-2026-0929.
